pipereader-advance-consumed-examined.title: Advance PipeReader consumed and examined positions correctly
pipereader-advance-consumed-examined.short: Distinguish parsed bytes from bytes inspected while retaining incomplete data
pipereader-advance-consumed-examined.summary: PipeReader requires consumers to report both the position fully consumed and the position examined in each ReadOnlySequence returned by ReadAsync.
pipereader-advance-consumed-examined.why: Incorrect positions can discard incomplete records or repeatedly inspect the same bytes, increasing work and retained memory.
pipereader-advance-consumed-examined.tips: Advance consumed only through complete records, retain incomplete tails, and set examined to the range actually inspected.

periodictimer-overlapping-work.title: Prevent overlapping periodic async work
periodictimer-overlapping-work.short: Do not start another callback while the previous iteration is still running
periodictimer-overlapping-work.summary: Callback timers can easily overlap asynchronous work when an iteration lasts longer than the interval; a single PeriodicTimer loop naturally serializes iterations.
periodictimer-overlapping-work.why: Overlapping iterations can multiply load, race on shared state, and make exceptions harder to observe.
periodictimer-overlapping-work.tips: When overlap is not intended, own the timer in one loop, await each iteration, and bind cancellation to the same lifetime.

task-waitasync-timeout-ownership.title: Separate Task.WaitAsync timeout from operation lifetime
task-waitasync-timeout-ownership.short: Stopping a wait does not necessarily stop the underlying Task
task-waitasync-timeout-ownership.summary: A timeout from Task.WaitAsync ends the caller's wait, but the operation represented by the original Task may continue running.
task-waitasync-timeout-ownership.why: Ignoring the continuing operation can race cleanup or retries and leave multiple copies of the same work active.
task-waitasync-timeout-ownership.tips: Decide explicitly whether the caller only abandons the wait or also owns cancellation of the operation through a CancellationToken.

priorityqueue-priority-semantics.title: Model element ordering with PriorityQueue priorities
priorityqueue-priority-semantics.short: Keep queued values separate from the priority used for dequeue order
priorityqueue-priority-semantics.summary: PriorityQueue<TElement,TPriority> maintains elements according to a separately compared priority and is useful when insertions and best-candidate removals are interleaved.
priorityqueue-priority-semantics.why: Sorting an entire List before every removal performs unnecessary repeated ordering work.
priorityqueue-priority-semantics.tips: Confirm the priority direction and include an additional sequence component when strict FIFO ordering among equal priorities is required.

random-shared-concurrent-generation.title: Use Random.Shared for shared non-cryptographic randomness
random-shared-concurrent-generation.short: Avoid constructing or externally locking Random instances just for concurrency
random-shared-concurrent-generation.summary: Random.Shared provides a shared Random instance intended for general-purpose pseudo-random generation from multiple threads.
random-shared-concurrent-generation.why: Repeatedly constructing Random instances or wrapping one shared instance in application locks adds unnecessary state management or contention.
random-shared-concurrent-generation.tips: Use it for simulation and ordinary sampling; use cryptographic randomness when unpredictability is a security property.

async-disposable-cleanup-lifetime.title: Await asynchronous disposal to close resource lifetime
async-disposable-cleanup-lifetime.short: Wait for asynchronous flush or close work when leaving scope
async-disposable-cleanup-lifetime.summary: IAsyncDisposable represents resources whose cleanup can itself be asynchronous, and await using waits for DisposeAsync when the scope exits.
async-disposable-cleanup-lifetime.why: Proceeding without awaiting cleanup can dispose dependent resources while a flush, protocol shutdown, or other asynchronous finalization is still running.
async-disposable-cleanup-lifetime.tips: Make ownership scopes explicit and check whether each API contracts synchronous disposal, asynchronous disposal, or both.

regex-capture-allocation-hot-path.title: Avoid unnecessary regex result allocations in hot paths
regex-capture-allocation-hot-path.short: Do not retain Match objects or strings when only positions are needed
regex-capture-allocation-hot-path.summary: Materializing and retaining regex Match results or extracted strings can create managed allocations proportional to the number of matches.
regex-capture-allocation-hot-path.why: Existence or position-only scans can create avoidable GC pressure when they materialize richer result objects.
regex-capture-allocation-hot-path.tips: Determine the information actually required and, on supporting runtimes, consider allocation-conscious iteration such as EnumerateMatches and verify gains with benchmarks.

aspnetcore-response-started-error-bounda.title: Do not rewrite ASP.NET Core errors after the response has started
aspnetcore-response-started-error-bounda.short: Status and headers cannot be safely replaced after they are sent
aspnetcore-response-started-error-bounda.summary: Once ASP.NET Core has started a response, a downstream failure generally cannot be converted into a fresh 500 response from the beginning.
aspnetcore-response-started-error-bounda.why: Exception middleware that assumes status and headers are always mutable can throw again or corrupt streaming responses.
aspnetcore-response-started-error-bounda.tips: Treat HasStarted as a boundary: generate the standard error before it, and define separate logging or connection behavior for failures after it.

unity-native-container-job-dependency-li.title: Keep Unity NativeContainers alive through dependent Jobs
unity-native-container-job-dependency-li.short: Align native-memory lifetime with JobHandle completion
unity-native-container-job-dependency-li.summary: A NativeArray or other NativeContainer passed to a Job must remain valid until that Job and dependent Jobs have finished using it.
unity-native-container-job-dependency-li.why: Disposing immediately after scheduling lets later Job execution access released native memory, causing safety exceptions or invalid memory access.
unity-native-container-job-dependency-li.tips: Track the use through JobHandle dependencies and dispose after completion or use disposal mechanisms integrated with the dependency chain.

unmanagedcallersonly-callback-boundary.title: Expose direct native callbacks with UnmanagedCallersOnly
unmanagedcallersonly-callback-boundary.short: Understand the constraints of callbacks that bypass managed delegates
unmanagedcallersonly-callback-boundary.summary: UnmanagedCallersOnlyAttribute can expose a static method for invocation from unmanaged code through a compatible function pointer.
unmanagedcallersonly-callback-boundary.why: Treating it like an ordinary managed method ignores constraints around calling conventions, parameter types, and managed invocation.
unmanagedcallersonly-callback-boundary.tips: Keep the blittable boundary small, prevent exceptions from escaping across it, and separate this direction of interop from imports such as LibraryImport.
